I saved the Q3 2025 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run the same way on Q2, my calculation reproduces all 10 reference values you gave me.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 308,738,043원 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 243 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 399,933,245원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u217@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 230 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 703,476원 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -16.3% |

To match the Q2 reference, I had to handle three things in the data that your definitions didn't spell out:

1. **Order dates are in UTC.** Assigning months and quarters by UTC gave Q2 results that didn't match the reference. Converting to Korea time (UTC+9) first made them match, so I used Korea time.
2. **Some customers have two accounts with the same email.** One email can have two customer IDs (e.g. u102@ex.com and u109@ex.com). For the customer counts (b, f) and refund totals (e), I treated one email as one customer. Counting by ID gave b=274 and f=217 for Q2, which doesn't match the reference of 228 and 190.
3. **Segment names are inconsistent.** Values like `SMB`, `smb`, ` consumer` and `Enterprise ` differ only in spacing and capitalisation, so I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping.

STATUS: DONE
